kaps_punt: Voedsel wat mense eet - vanaf plante en diere (klassifikasie)

items.bewering: Die kos op jou bord het nie in die winkel begin nie.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: Stats SA, Census of Commercial Agriculture 2017 (statssa.gov.za/?p=13144): food is produced on 40 122 commercial farms (livestock, field crops, horticulture, mixed) before it reaches retail; FAO calorie-share data below.

items.bewering: Die meeste van ons kos word eers op 'n plaas gekweek of grootgemaak.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: FAO calorie-supply shares as tabulated in National Academies document pga_062632 (sites.nationalacademies.org): cereals, oils, sugar, roots, pulses and livestock products supply about 99% of global calories; fish under 1%. 'Die meeste' is the right quantifier: wild-caught fish and foraged food are the exceptions.

items.bewering: Party boere kweek plante, party hou diere aan en ander doen albei.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: Stats SA, Census of Commercial Agriculture 2017 (statssa.gov.za/?p=13144; gov.za media statement 24 March 2020): livestock farming 33.9% of farms, mixed farming 31.1%, field crops 21.3%.

items.bewering: Ons noem hierdie werk boerdery.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: Merriam-Webster 'farm': land used for growing crops or raising livestock; Oxford Learner's 'farm': used for growing crops and/or keeping animals. In context 'hierdie werk' refers to growing plants or keeping animals, which matches.

items.bewering: Daarom kom die meeste van ons kos van plante of van diere af.
items.blok: Kos begin nie in die winkel nie
items.bron: Same FAO calorie shares (National Academies pga_062632): virtually all dietary energy comes from plant and animal products. The 'daarom' chain holds because farming is growing plants or keeping animals; farmed mushrooms (a fungus) are an exception, which 'die meeste' covers.

items.bewering: Mielies groei op 'n lang plant met groot blare. Ons eet die pitte wat aan die mieliekop sit.
items.bron: New World Encyclopedia 'Maize'; Lucidcentral Tropical Forages 'Zea mays' (apps.lucidcentral.org): plant 1-4 m (commercial about 2.5 m), leaves 50-100 cm long and 5-10 cm wide; 200-400 kernels set along the cob of each ear.

items.bewering: 'n Appel is die vrug wat aan die takke van 'n appelboom groei.
items.bron: Museum fuer Naturkunde Berlin, Naturblick 'Malus domestica'; Wikipedia 'Apple': the apple is the fruit (a pome) of the apple tree, borne on its branches.

items.bewering: By 'n wortel eet ons die deel van die plant wat onder die grond groei.
items.bron: NParks Singapore Flora & Fauna Web, Daucus carota (nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/5/9/5923): the edible part is the swollen taproot, which grows in the soil. The shoulder may show at the surface; that does not make the claim false at this level.

items.bewering: Koring is 'n plant met klein korrels bo-aan sy stingel.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Wheat'; Farmer's Weekly 'The basics of wheat': the grains form in a terminal spike (ear) at the top of the stem.

items.bewering: Die meeste brood word van koring gemaak.
items.bron: Grain SA, 'What is a wheat producer's percentage share of retail white bread' (grainsa.co.za); World Grain, 'Wheat milling in South Africa': South African bread is baked from wheat flour (white and brown bread flour), about 2.8 billion loaves a year. Rye and maize breads exist, so 'die meeste' is correct.

items.bewering: Daarom tel brood ook as kos van 'n plant.
items.bron: Follows from the wheat-flour sources above: the main ingredient of bread is milled wheat. Yeast is a fungus, the same group the lesson puts mushrooms in, but it is a minor ingredient and the lesson does not mention it. Bread is conventionally classed as a plant food. Nothing a learner meets in this lesson conflicts with it.

items.bewering: Die melk wat ons drink en waarvan ons kaas en botter maak, kom van diere af.
items.bron: Agricultural Product Standards Act 119 of 1990, Regulation R260 (2015) on dairy and imitation dairy products (acts.co.za; DALRRD notice via ascfoodsafety.com): in South Africa 'milk' on its own is a dairy product from animals; plant drinks are 'imitation' or '(plant name) milk'. A learner who applies the lesson's tracing rule to soy or almond milk correctly gets 'plant', so there is no conflict.

items.bewering: In Suid-Afrika kom hierdie melk veral van koeie.
items.bron: Milk SA figures reported by agriland.ie ('South Africa's dairy industry likely to grow'): commercial dairy herd of about 1.27 million cows (Holstein, Jersey); DALRRD 'Goat Milk' agro-processing document: goat milk is a small niche and goats are mostly kept informally.

items.bewering: Vleis kom ook van diere, soos beeste, skape en hoenders.
items.bron: DALRRD statistical information and Farming Portal 'Meat consumption in South Africa continues to surge': poultry about 60% of meat eaten, beef about 30%, then pork and mutton/lamb (about 170 000 t produced).

items.bewering: Die eiers wat ons eet, kom meestal van hoenders af.
items.bron: FAO, Poultry sector country review South Africa (fao.org/3/a-ax256e.pdf): about 29.7 million layer hens on commercial farms; DALRRD Egg Market Value Chain Profile 2021: the egg industry is hens' eggs (about 486 000 t in 2023). Other eggs (ostrich, duck) exist, so 'meestal' is correct.

items.bewering: Kaas groei nie self nie en word deur mense van melk gemaak.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Cheesemaking' and 'Cheese'; Wisconsin Cheese 'What is rennet?': cheese is made by people who curdle milk with acid and rennet and separate the curd from the whey.

items.bewering: Die melk kom van 'n dier soos 'n koei of 'n bok. Daarom is kaas ook kos van 'n dier.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Cheese': usually from the milk of cows, goats or sheep; Farmer's Weekly 'Better milk, better cheese from veld-reared goats' and taste.co.za 'chevin': goat's milk cheese is made in South Africa.

items.bewering: Tog lyk die meeste kaas glad nie soos melk nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Cheesemaking': cheese is the pressed, often aged solid curd, while milk is a liquid. Soft white cheeses such as cottage cheese are whitish but still not liquid, and 'die meeste' covers them.

items.bewering: Jy kan die meeste kos self in een van hierdie twee groepe sorteer.
items.bron: True for single foods and ingredients, by the FAO calorie shares above (nearly everything eaten is a plant or animal product). See the separate onseker item on mixed foods.

items.bewering: Volg die kos terug tot by die plant of die dier wat dit gemaak of gegee het. As jy by 'n plant uitkom, is dit kos van 'n plant. As jy by 'n dier uitkom, is dit kos van 'n dier.
items.bron: Tested on cases a learner might try: honey goes back to the bee that made it, so animal (correct; honey is an animal product, vegnews.com 'Why do bees make honey'). Sugar goes back to sugar cane, so plant. Eggs go to the hen and milk to the cow. Soy milk goes to a plant (R260 above). Salt reaches neither, which agrees with the next block. Mushrooms: a learner may think they 'grow like plants' and say plant, but the next block explicitly heads that off. The rule gives the right answer for every single-origin food tried.

items.bewering: Die meeste kos wat ons eet, pas in een van hierdie twee groepe. Party kos pas egter in nie een van die twee nie. [read together with the tracing rule: 'Volg die kos terug tot by die plant of die dier ...']
items.blok: Kos wat nie in die twee groepe pas nie
items.nota: Every sentence here is true. The problem is the classification picture, and sources cannot settle that, which is why this is onseker and not a guess. The lesson offers three outcomes: plant, animal, or neither (salt, mushrooms). It has no outcome for food made from both. A learner who tries cake, pizza, a cheese sandwich or vetkoek with butter gets back to a plant AND an animal. Such a food does not fit 'in een van hierdie twee groepe', so the nearest slot the lesson offers is 'pas in nie een van die twee nie', next to salt and mushrooms. That would be wrong. A person should decide one of two things: either accept that the lesson classifies single foods/ingredients only, or have one short sentence added saying that food made from several things, such as cake, comes from plants and animals. The second option adds content under a word ceiling, so it is a scope call rather than a writer fix.

items.bewering: Botter word van melk gemaak en is dus kos van 'n dier.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Churning (butter)'; McGill Office for Science and Society 'How does milk become butter'; Dairysafe Victoria 'Butter': butter is churned from cream separated from milk (or from whole milk).

items.bewering: Grondboontjiebotter word van grondboontjies gemaak en is dus kos van 'n plant.
items.bron: Peanut butter is ground roasted peanuts, with salt, sugar or vegetable oil sometimes added and no dairy (manufacturer ingredient lists, e.g. Whole Earth, Pip & Nut). The peanut is the seed of a legume plant (Arachis hypogaea).

items.bewering: Die twee name klink amper dieselfde, maar die kos begin by heeltemal verskillende plekke.
items.bron: Follows from the two items above: butter comes from an animal (the cow's milk) and peanut butter from a plant (the peanut). 'Heeltemal verskillende' is accurate at the level of plant against animal.

items.bewering: Die meeste kos wat ons eet, pas in een van hierdie twee groepe. Party kos pas egter in nie een van die twee nie.
items.blok: Kos wat nie in die twee groepe pas nie
items.bron: FAO calorie shares (National Academies pga_062632): nearly all food is a plant or animal product; salt, water and fungi are the exceptions. True as stated for single foods. The mixed-food gap is a separate item.

items.bewering: Sout kom uit die see of uit die grond en was nooit 'n plant of 'n dier nie.
items.blok: Kos wat nie in die twee groepe pas nie
items.bron: Walvis Bay Salt, Salt Forum 2023 presentation (imformed.com): South African salt comes from coastal works (Velddrif, Coega, Swartkops), Northern Cape inland pans (about 400 000 t of about 700 000 t) and Namibian sea-salt imports; Mail & Guardian 'Salt: the journey from mine to meal' (2015): Kalahari pan salt is underground brine pumped up and evaporated. Salt is the mineral sodium chloride. 'Nooit' holds.

items.bewering: Sampioene lyk soos plante, maar hulle is nie plante of diere nie.
items.blok: Kos wat nie in die twee groepe pas nie
items.bron: Forest Preserve District of Will County 'Five fabulous facts about fungi' (reconnectwithnature.org): fungi form their own kingdom, separate from plants and animals, and do not photosynthesise; SATNT (Suid-Afrikaanse Tydskrif vir Natuurwetenskap en Tegnologie) article on Afrikaans and English names for South African mushrooms and macrofungi treats them as fungi (swamme). The comparison 'lyk soos plante' is immediately corrected in the same sentence, so its mapping does not mislead.

items.bewering: boerdery: Om plante te kweek en diere aan te hou vir kos en ander produkte.
items.bron: Read alone, as a glossary entry is read, 'plante te kweek EN diere aan te hou' defines farming as doing both. Stats SA, Census of Commercial Agriculture 2017: two-thirds of South African commercial farms do only one (livestock 33.9%, field crops 21.3%, horticulture besides), and only 31.1% are mixed. The lesson's own first block says 'party boere kweek plante, party hou diere aan en ander doen albei'. Oxford Learner's uses 'and/or' and Merriam-Webster 'or' for exactly this reason. 'Vir kos en ander produkte' is correct (wool, cotton, flowers, timber).
items.regstelling: Make the definition say 'one or the other or both', e.g. 'Om plante te kweek of diere aan te hou, of albei, vir kos en ander produkte.' The writer should choose the wording. If this entry is a shared definition across lessons, the change belongs in the subject's agreed-wordings list and not in this lesson alone.

opsomming: 26 claims confirmed, including every 'die meeste', 'meestal', 'veral' and 'nooit', with plant, animal and neither tested as a set and the sorting rule tested on honey, sugar, soy milk, salt and mushrooms. A person must decide whether the lesson needs a line for food made from both plants and animals (cake, sandwich): its three-way plant/animal/neither picture leaves a learner nowhere to put such food except, wrongly, beside salt. Separately, the 'boerdery' glossary entry, read alone, says farming is growing plants AND keeping animals, while most South African farms do only one, so it should read 'or ... or both' (check first whether it is a shared wording).
